title: Child repos' CI runs the same claude-settings tools as local sessions, so a stale pin never costs a lane
why: Your gripe, Oct 26 ("doesn't this just mean CI is old? why would we conform"): a degen session spent two CI runs on a sentence that only the old pinned linter refused, nearly dropped the iPhone Duo record lane, then asked you to choose.
note: claude-settings part merged Oct 27 (PR 647, "ste-changed names the CI pin"; main e305bdbc). Left: the child-repo part below. bin/ste-changed now names the CI ste-lint pin and exits 3 when its lint files differ from the local copy. Rule git-integration-branch-merge: a CI lint red that ste-changed passes, while it blames an old ste-lint pin, is not a strike; the session moves the pin with no question. Decision action-pins-follow-sessions: no bot keeps pins current; Dependabot cannot bump them (read from dependabot-core source f0feb6f: no version tag in claude-settings, so no update; not run live). Old pins measured Oct 26: degen 95ada63, q_max 9d577ab, joyous 873704e (ste-lint); banchi ef49dde and q_max 8abab8d (stamp). Child-repo part (bump each repo's pins) deferred (shiv, Oct 26): you check each repo's plan first; it rides with the roll-out visits (r1). Port: yes, every repo that pins ste-lint gets the check through bin/ste-changed.
